The Straw Hat Jolly Roger from One Piece has become Gen Z’s symbol of protest across Asia. From Indonesia to Nepal and the Philippines, young people have adopted the pirate flag to challenge corruption and oppression. Its appeal lies in shared anime culture, a narrative of fighting tyranny, visual simplicity, political neutrality, and viral spread online. Despite crackdowns, the flag has grown more powerful, showing how Gen Z blends memes, humor, and pop culture to reshape modern protest.

data.text:
$GRAB Map (B2B) Discussion 🧵

TLDR: If you don't read until the end, you will miss the juicy part! GrabMap(B2B) is a big deal long term! 

Grab Maps is Free to use for Drivers/Users in the SuperApp,  is the in-house mapping and location intelligence platform developed by Grab Holdings Limited, the Southeast Asian super-app offering ride-hailing, deliveries, financial services, and more. Launched as an enterprise service in 2022, GrabMaps leverages hyperlocal data collected from Grab's vast network of drivers, riders, and delivery partners to provide accurate, real-time mapping tailored to the unique challenges of Southeast Asia's urban and rural landscapes, such as informal roads, traffic patterns, and points of interest not well-covered by global providers like Google Maps. It powers Grab's core operations while increasingly being offered as a B2B solution to external clients.

History of Grab Maps:

Grab's journey into mapping began as a necessity driven by operational inefficiencies and high costs associated with third-party mapping services. Founded in 2012 as MyTeksi (later rebranded to Grab in 2016), the company initially relied on providers like Google Maps and HERE Technologies for navigation in its ride-hailing services.

However, these global solutions proved inadequate for Southeast Asia's complex environments, including unmapped alleys, dynamic traffic, and hyperlocal points like street food stalls or informal addresses, leading to inaccuracies that frustrated drivers and users.

By 2018, Grab started addressing this by contributing to OpenStreetMap (OSM), an open-source mapping project. Contractors used satellite imagery to edit and "correct" map data in countries like Thailand, though this drew criticism from the OSM community for potentially introducing errors without on-ground verification.

This effort marked Grab's shift toward building proprietary mapping capabilities to reduce dependency on expensive licenses, which were costing the company millions annually amid rapid expansion

The pivotal moment came in 2022 when Grab announced it would fully power its services with its own mapping technology by Q3 of that year. 
GrabMaps was officially launched as an enterprise service, already supporting operations in seven of Grab's eight markets (Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, Cambodia, and Myanmar). This in-house system used data from over 10 million daily rides and deliveries to create hyperlocal maps, aiming to tap into a $1 billion annual market opportunity for location-based services in Southeast Asia. The development was led by teams focusing on AI-driven data collection, including custom cameras mounted on vehicles to capture street-level imagery. 

The Progress of Grab Maps and AI Integration:

~AI and Machine Learning Enhancements: In November 2024, Grab partnered with OpenAI to fine-tune GPT-4o vision models for better localization of traffic signs (speed limits, turn restrictions), road geometries, and places. This reduced manual mapping efforts and improved accuracy in complex urban settings. By 2024, Grab deployed hundreds of AI/ML models across its mapping tools, earning awards for innovation. 

~Hardware Innovations: In April 2025, Grab launched the KartaCam 2, an edge AI-powered camera that builds on earlier models like KartaCam. It enables real-time data capture for mapping, with enhanced processing for low-light conditions and dynamic environments. By the end of 2025, Grab plans to deploy around 20,000 such cameras across Southeast Asia, crowdsourcing data from drivers to keep maps updated. 

~ Partnerships and Expansions: In May 2025, Grab collaborated with Natix, a Solana-based DePIN (Decentralized Physical Infrastructure Network) project, to integrate crowdsourced mapping for autonomous driving applications. This rewards users for contributing data, aiming to "reshape" mapping in the region.A major milestone came in October 2025, when GrabMaps partnered with Tino, Mongolia's super-app, to build the country's first advanced digital map—marking GrabMaps' first full-country project outside Southeast Asia. This expansion signals ambitions to compete globally with players like Google Maps. 

~Autonomous Vehicle (AV) Integration: GrabMaps is positioning itself as a key enabler for AV transitions, providing rich datasets from millions of real-world driving hours, traffic flows, and heat maps. 
investing.comIn 2025 earnings discussions, Grab highlighted upcoming AV pilots and partnerships with global AI firms, leveraging GrabMaps for regulatory compliance and operational efficiency. 

GrabMaps' cost savings are more impactful than direct revenue. By internalizing mapping, Grab has avoided tens of millions in annual fees, contributing to overall profitability improvements—e.g., Grab turned profitable in Q2 2025 with $10M net profit. It also save drivers 15-20% fuel on average, which led to higher income. 

Ok, now the Juicy Part, How much Revenue GrabMap will be able to generate long term?

1. Grab can place Ads for businesses within the Maps interface, which users may see when searching/using for direction(that is why it is free for users)

2. Promoted Listings: Businesses will pay to have their icon/logo/brand/listings appear more highlighted on the GrabMap, especially for searches for local services. 

3. GrabMap APIs: Grab can charge businesses for access to its APIs(Application Programming Interfaces), which allow developers to integrate GrabMap into their App/Website

4. Commissions and Integrations: GrabMap can earn revenue through partnership like currently with @Microsoft , @amazon , @Huawei, taking in commission and licensing fees.

5. Subscription service: GrabMap can offer subscription plans for businesses or developers that seeking advanced features, support or customization.

6. Data and Users accumulation: The extensive or massive amount of data collected from users will be helpful to build new products or improve ads targeting to GradAds segment.

Long Term, GrabMap can bring in $10-$15B or more a year( @Google makes around $20-$25B a year off @googlemaps). Mapping in SEA or Bottom of Pyramid regions are complex and difficult. It requires innovation and billions of data points to accurately re-design a complete Map solution, which is what @AnthonyPY_Tan and Grab Team already acomplished.  The recent expansion with  Tino to build GrabMap in Mongolia confirmed Anthony ambition.
